import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the dataset
data = pd.read_csv('data/customer_segments.csv')

# Create a figure and a set of subplots
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))

# Calculate total spending for each customer and add as a new column
data['Total_Spending'] = data['MntWines'] + data['MntFruits'] + data['MntMeatProducts'] + \
                         data['MntFishProducts'] + data['MntSweetProducts'] + data['MntGoldProds']

# Plot a boxplot to visualize the distribution of total spending by education level
sns.boxplot(x='Education', y='Total_Spending', data=data, palette='Set2')

# Set plot title and labels
plt.title('Total Spending Distribution by Education Level', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Education Level', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Total Spending', fontsize=12)

# Save the plot
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the dataset
data = pd.read_csv('data/customer_segments.csv')

# Create a figure and a set of subplots
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))

# Calculate total spending for each customer and add as a new column
data['Total_Spending'] = data['MntWines'] + data['MntFruits'] + data['MntMeatProducts'] + \
                         data['MntFishProducts'] + data['MntSweetProducts'] + data['MntGoldProds']

# Plot a boxplot to visualize the distribution of total spending by education level
sns.boxplot(x='Education', y='Total_Spending', data=data, palette='Set2')

# Set plot title and labels
plt.title('Total Spending Distribution by Education Level', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Education Level', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Total Spending', fontsize=12)

# Save the plot
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
